verdict.rationale: Bento's hosted MCP server and CLI let an agent create broadcasts, and the Broadcasts API supports campaigns aimed at a saved segment that can be scheduled with explicit audience rules. The phrase "schedule approved sends" implies a human-approval step, but no draft or pending-approval state is documented, nor any mechanism that holds an agent-created broadcast until a human signs off. missing for 10: documented draft/approval-queue state for agent-created broadcasts, explicit human-approval gate before send, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can draft a campaign against a segment and leave it scheduled or queued for a human to approve before send

citations.quote: It can look up subscribers, create broadcasts, track events, and more, all through natural conversation.
Broadcasts are one-time marketing sends to a broad audience or a saved segment. Use the API to review broadcast history, create campaigns, and schedule approved sends with explicit audience rules.
